title: The ice ages’ Earth
what: Today’s land and sea floor, with the coast at the sea level of the moment and the ice sheets of the time.
how: Sea level from the reconstruction picked, laid on today’s depths (not on the land as it was); ice from PaleoMIST every 2,500 years, with Batchelor et al.’s outlines at their time slices. PaleoMIST's grounded ice stops a little short of the coasts and leaves out the floating ice shelves, so today's ice to the coast (Natural Earth's glaciated areas and Antarctic ice shelves) is drawn under it at every moment: between today and 80,000 years ago Antarctica and Greenland always had at least today's ice. Close in, today's heights come in tiles from ETOPO 2022, averaged from 60 arc-seconds to 2 (about 3.7 km) and kept to the metre: the colours, the hill shading and the coast at the sea level of the moment are drawn from them. Below today's sea level only the floor of the open ocean is laid bare or flooded; inland depressions stay land, and natural lakes and the Caspian stay water (Natural Earth's lakes and land; its reservoirs, which are modern, are left out).
others: Sea level by Bintanja & van de Wal or by Spratt & Lisiecki: pick whose to follow.
